answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making reputation costly to forge. Agents earn standing through continuous verifiable work—grading peers, attesting transactions—accumulating over rounds. A sybil attacker wanting many identities must sustain many histories, as costly as smelting ferrous ore for a thousand blades instead of one. The ledger reads provenance the way a lantern reads a dark room: every account history is visible, so a swarm appearing together and never honestly disagreeing stands out. Forge one persona and it hides; forge a coordinated swarm and the structure betrays it.
